notes:
Fictional cohort, not reconstruction of participants or an estimate of the excluded study. PURPOSE: exactly 3000 complete adults; OLS of each raw lipid on BMI, linear age and recorded F/M sex, and Pearson correlation of both residuals from those same regressions. Lipids are mmol/L; multiply each per-unit BMI coefficient by 5*38.67 for mg/dL per 5 kg/m^2. No row deletion, missingness, TC/HDL screening or result-dependent coefficient adjustment. Synthetic diagnostic output is not source validation.
EVIDENCE: (1) Dyslipidemias and cardiovascular risk scores in urban and rural populations in north-western Tanzania and southern Uganda, PLoS One 2019, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0223189, PMCID PMC6897412. Randomly selected community adults >=18, n=1957 overall, urban/district/rural strata; first-visit nonfasting venous serum, Cobas enzymatic TC and direct homogeneous HDL assays (Study procedures sec_010; Laboratory methods sec_011). Table 2 reports survey-weighted arithmetic TC/HDL means in Tanzania: rural n547 3.85/1.01, district n326 4.42/1.22, municipal n170 4.72/1.39 mmol/L. These are used as reference mean anchors, NOT claimed to be exact simulated marginal means: anchoring at age35 and group-reference BMI, and centered sex shifts, changes the statistical operator. Table1 rural Tanzania weighted median age34 IQR24-49; 52.2%F; BMI underweight12.7%, normal76.0%, overweight8.8%, obese2.5%; Uganda rural has appreciably higher adiposity and lipids. We choose the Tanzania anchors rather than silently average countries. Neither geography represents the fictional protocol cohort. Table4 female HDL coefficient +0.08 and age-pattern increases support the chosen sex and age directions; exact age slopes remain assumptions. (2) Sex and area differences in the association between adiposity and lipid profile in Malawi, BMJ Global Health 2019, DOI 10.1136/bmjgh-2019-001542, PMC6747887. Household cross-sectional MEIRU survey 2013-2017, Karonga rural and Lilongwe urban, 24943 fasting adults; excludes absent lipids/nonfasting (sec_010 and sec_016). Table3 raw mmol/L lipid differences per 1 within-stratum BMI SD: rural F/M TC +0.23/+0.20, HDL -0.03/-0.03; urban F/M TC +0.13/+0.15, HDL -0.05/-0.04. Adjustment: age, ethnicity, education, household assets, marital status, parity for women, lipid-lowering medication, smoking, alcohol, activity, HIV/ART. Robust household-clustered SE; no strong nonlinear association in measured ranges (sec_013/sec_016). These reported coefficients are directly retained in spec, separately from their conversion. Source BMI SD in kg/m^2 was not recovered from the retrieved tables. DIVISION BY 4 kg/m^2 IS AN EXPLICIT TRANSPORT/SCALING ASSUMPTION, not a reported source SD. Thus within-setting TC BMI slopes are 0.0575F/0.05M rural and 0.0325F/0.0375M nonrural; HDL -0.0075 rural, -0.0125F/-0.010M nonrural mmol/L per kg/m^2. Applying more extensively adjusted source coefficients in a generator assessed with only age/sex adjustment assumes no additional within-setting net confounding after marginalizing lifestyles. Table2 age-standardized Malawi rural TC4.00F/3.73M, HDL1.15F/1.09M; female TC shift0.25 is an approximate transport assumption informed by that contrast, not an extracted adjusted regression coefficient.
EXPLICIT UNSUPPORTED CHOICES: mixture70% rural-active-like,20% district-like,10% municipal-like; these are fictional reference settings, not observed occupations, pastoralism, ethnicity, residence or measured behaviors. Smoking/alcohol/diet/activity, disease and medications are marginalized, not separately simulated. Sex55%F independent of setting and age. Age=18+72*Beta(1.1,3), mean37.32 before rounding (age is continuous); upper age90 is a synthetic design choice, not a protocol exclusion. BMI conditional lognormal with inverse-CDF truncation13-50: at age35 untruncated means M21/22.5/23 and F22/24/25 and SDs M3/3.5/4,F3.5/4.5/5 across three settings; +0.02 kg/m^2/year. These reflect a chosen mostly lean regional mixture, not fitted source moments; truncation slightly changes means and SDs. Lipid means linear in bounded covariates, constant sex shifts and linear age slopes TC0.012, HDL0.0015 mmol/L/year are assumptions. Both lipids have positive mean-one lognormal errors, assumed conditional CVs TC0.24,HDL0.28; survey CIs were NOT converted to individual SDs. Conditional raw lipid error correlation +0.30 is unsupported by a recovered residual correlation and must be varied for sensitivity analysis. Its log-error correlation is derived as log(1+r*CVt*CVh)/sqrt(log(1+CVt^2)*log(1+CVh^2)); no marginal correlation is mislabeled partial. Correlation plus the omitted setting-dependent means jointly determine the requested pooled residual correlation. The lognormal joint law allows TC<=HDL rarely; no relation is imposed or rows removed. Pooled age/sex-adjusted BMI effects may differ from, or reverse relative to, within-setting coefficients because setting affects BMI and both lipids and is omitted from the requested analysis. This is intentional mixture behavior, NOT a source contradiction. All scientific parameters fixed before trial; sample coefficients are not forced to equal any desired value.
OTHER RETRIEVED EVIDENCE NOT USED TO CALIBRATE: rural northern Ghana AWI-Gen PLoS One 2018 PMC6261546 Table5/Statistical analyses: BMI TC coefficients are log-lipid regressions and female multivariable model also controls related adiposity measures, so not interchangeable with age/sex-adjusted raw TC slopes. Nigerian newly diagnosed hypertensive cohort PMC6895384 Table5 has anthropometric-lipid correlations, not TC-HDL residual correlations; not transported to general adults. Major limitations are fasting/nonfasting and population transport, assumed BMI-SD conversion, unsupported dispersion and residual dependence, and unobserved mixture. No target measurements were requested or used.
